description: Issue #830: the Heritage `value of … for key …` reader must be reachable INSIDE parentheses, which `spec/grammar.md` derives — `primary` (:193-204) offers both `parenthesized-expression` (:199, defined :213) and `value-of-reader` (:203, defined :217), so `( value of :d for key "a" )` is a `parenthesized-expression` wrapping a `value-of-reader`. It once raised `ol-bad-token`: the `(` path took `value` as a `parenthesized-call` callee (:215) and never entered the reader. #885 fixed that incidentally by deriving `NON_PRIMARY_NAMES` from the keyword registry (which contains `value`), so `isCalleeName` rejects it and the `(` path falls through — but nothing pinned it, so a future edit to that derivation would silently restore the defect. This fixture pins the PARSE + SEMANTIC stages clean across every parenthesized shape: the reader wholly parenthesized, as its own dictionary operand, as its own key operand, redundantly grouped, composed with infix `+`, and carrying `.field`/`[selector]` postfixes (proving it is a real `primary`, :192). Its execution twin is `heritage/execution/heritage-value-of-key-reader-in-parentheses`, because `execute()` never calls `check()`. The reader operates on a dict, so Heritage also needs Data (`spec/conformance.md:301`).
